findings.title: Raw-HTML posts bypass HTML sanitization
findings.body: Post#cook returns the stored raw text verbatim for the new raw_html cook method, and TopicEmbed uses that method for imported content. The feed-polling path passes arbitrary RSS/Atom HTML directly to TopicEmbed without Readability's tag whitelist or any other sanitizer, after which the result is stored as cooked HTML and rendered raw. A malicious or compromised feed item containing script tags, event-handler attributes, or other active markup therefore becomes stored XSS for forum visitors. Imported HTML must be passed through a whitelist sanitizer before it is saved as cooked content.

findings.title: Imported URL is interpolated unescaped into stored HTML
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import builds the 'Imported from' anchor by inserting the supplied URL directly into an HTML string, both as the href attribute value and as the link text. The only earlier check is that the string starts with http:// or https://, so a URL containing quotes or angle brackets can break out of the anchor and inject arbitrary markup. Because the resulting post uses raw_html rendering, that injected markup is stored and served without sanitization. The URL and link text must be HTML/attribute escaped, or the anchor must be built with a DOM builder.

findings.title: Remote import performs unrestricted server-side fetching
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read before TopicEmbed.import performs its scheme check, with no timeout, response-size limit, or restriction on redirect targets or private IP addresses. The on-demand retrieval flow validates only the initial URL's host, while open-uri follows HTTP redirects, so an embeddable-host URL can redirect the server to localhost, link-local, or internal services and have the fetched content converted into a public topic; a very large response is also read entirely into memory. Fetching needs an explicit HTTP(S) client with scheme/final-URI validation, private-address blocking, timeouts, and a size cap.

findings.title: Feed polling crashes on items without full content
findings.body: poll_feed unconditionally calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. Many RSS/Atom items provide only a description or summary and no content/content:encoded element, in which case i.content is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The job is configured with retry: false and has no per-item error handling, so one such item aborts the entire hourly import and prevents all remaining items from being processed. The code should fall back to description/summary when content is absent and isolate failures per item.

findings.title: Unknown embed URLs enqueue unbounded background jobs
findings.body: Every request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, and the loading page automatically reloads and repeats the request. The Referer check is trivially spoofable by non-browser clients, and TopicRetriever's 60-second throttle is only applied after a job is dequeued, so an attacker can flood Sidekiq with jobs and use distinct URLs on the embeddable host to trigger repeated outbound fetch attempts. Host validation and an atomic throttle/deduplication check need to happen before enqueueing, with throttled requests returning the loading response without creating another job.

findings.title: Embed creation has a check-then-create race
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import first queries for an existing embed and then creates the topic, post, and embed record without any locking. The scheduled feed poller and an on-demand RetrieveTopic job (or two concurrent retrieves) can both observe no embed for the same URL and both create content; the loser then hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url at create! and the whole job fails with RecordNotUnique even though the URL was successfully imported by the winner. Creation should be made atomic or rescue RecordNotUnique and return the existing embed's post.

findings.title: Disqus import now depends on live thread URLs and drops the category option
findings.body: The importer previously created each topic locally from the Disqus export, but now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which fetches t[:link] over the network for every thread. If a linked article has moved, returns 404, or the import runs offline, open() raises and aborts the entire import, losing comments that are fully present in the export file. The same change removes the --category Thor option, breaking existing import invocations that pass it and leaving no way to place imported threads in a category. The export-based creation needs to remain as a fallback and the category option needs to be plumbed through to topic creation.

findings.title: Only root-relative URLs are absolutized in imported content
findings.body: absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Relative references such as 'images/photo.jpg' or 'page2.html', which are common in feed content, are left unchanged and will resolve against the Discourse host instead of the source article, producing broken images and links. Conversely, a protocol-relative URL like '//cdn.example.com/x.js' starts with '/' and is incorrectly rewritten onto the article's host. All non-absolute references should be resolved with URI.join against the source URL, which handles relative, root-relative, and protocol-relative forms correctly.

findings.title: postMessage origin is validated by substring matching
findings.body: The resize handler trusts a message when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the sender's origin merely appears as a substring of the configured Discourse URL. For example, when discourseUrl includes a port such as https://forum.example.com:3000/, a page served from the distinct origin https://forum.example.com (default port) passes the check and can drive the iframe's height. The handler should parse discourseUrl, extract its exact origin, and require strict equality with e.origin.

findings.title: Feed-setting guard specs pass without exercising the guards
findings.body: The specs for 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' stub only the setting named in the example. Jobs::PollFeed#execute checks feed_polling_enabled? first, and that setting defaults to false, so execute short-circuits before the stubbed setting is ever consulted and poll_feed is never called regardless of whether the URL/username guards exist. These examples would still pass if those two guards were deleted. Each example needs the preceding conditions stubbed to their enabling values (enabled true, and a present URL for the username example) so only the guard under test can block polling.
